description: An accordion is a vertical stack of interactive headings used to toggle the display of further information; each item can be 'collapsed' with just a short label visible or 'expanded' to show the full content.
A way of informing the user of important changes in a prominent way.
A link that allows users to navigate from one location to another within the same page. Anchor links are often used to implement in-page tables of contents.
A graphical representation of a user: usually a photo, illustration, or initial.
A small label, generally appearing inside or in close proximity to another larger interface component, representing a status, property, or some other metadata.
A list of links showing the location of the current page in the navigational hierarchy.
A wrapper for multiple, related buttons.

A type of menu that appears on demand and contains a small set of relevant actions related to a control, an area of the interface, a piece of data in the application, or a view of the application. In mouse-driven interfaces, contextual menus are often triggered by a right click on an item of interest.
A means of displaying multiple slides of content, one or more at a time. Navigation between slides can be controlled via swiping, scrolling, or buttons.
An input for choosing from predefined options: when used alone, it gives a binary choice (checked/unchecked); in a group it allows the user to select multiple values from a list of options.
An input for choosing a color.
An input that behaves similarly to a select, with the addition of a free text input to filter options.
A means of inputting a date – often separated into multiple individual fields for day/month/year.
A visual way to choose a date using a calendar view.
A panel which slides out from the edge of the screen.
A menu in which options are hidden by default but can be shown by interacting with a button; it differs from a select in that it shows actions or navigation options and is not a form input.
An indication to the user that there is no data to display in the current view; it often includes an alternative action (e.g. try a different search term).
A wrapper for related form fields.
A representation of a file such as an uploaded attachment or a downloadable PDF.
An input which allows users to upload a file from their device.
Commonly appearing at the bottom of a page or section, a footer is used to display copyright and legal information or links to related content.
A grouping of input controls that allow a user to submit information to a server.
An element that appears across the top of all pages on a website or application; it usually contains the site name and main navigation.
A title or caption used to introduce a new section.
Text appearing alongside or below a form input to provide additional context or guidance.
A line used to visually separate content within a page.
A symbol used to communicate functionality or provide visual cues.
A visual representation such as a photo, illustration, or graphic.
A visual representation of a key on a keyboard, often used in documentation to show shortcuts.
An interactive element used for navigation between pages or sections.
A series of related items, either ordered or unordered.
An animation used to indicate that an action or content is being processed or loaded.
A list of actions or options that a user can choose from.
A dialog box or window that appears on top of the main content, requiring user interaction before they can return to the main application.
An input that allows users to select multiple options from a predefined list.
An input field specifically for entering numbers, often with controls to increment or decrement the value.
A series of links used to navigate across multiple pages of content.
A secure text input that masks the characters entered.
A visual representation of the completion status of a process or task.
A control that allows a user to select only one option from a set of mutually exclusive choices.
A text input designed for entering search queries.
A form element that allows users to choose one option from a dropdown list.
A placeholder used to represent content that is still loading, giving a visual hint of the layout.
A link used by keyboard users to skip directly to the main content of a page, bypassing repetitive navigation.
An input for choosing a value from a range by moving a handle along a track.
A visual indicator for progress through a multi-step workflow.
A toggle used to turn a specific setting or feature on or off.
A structured display for data organized into rows and columns.
A navigation component used to switch between different views within the same context.
A small label used for categorization or to represent a keyword.
A multi-line text input field.
A single-line text input field.
A brief, non-persistent notification providing feedback on an action.
An input that allows the user to switch between two states, such as on and off.
A small informational pop-up that appears when hovering over or focusing on an element.
A hierarchical list often used for folder structures or navigation menus.
An element used for embedding and playing video content.
A technique to hide content visually while keeping it accessible to screen readers.
